{{Short description|Partial differential equation}}
The '''Swift–Hohenberg equation''' (named after Jack B. Swift and [[Pierre Hohenberg]]) is a [[partial differential equation]] noted for its pattern-forming behaviour. It takes the form

:<math>
\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = r u - (1+\nabla^2)^2u + N(u)
</math>

where ''u'' = ''u''(''x'', ''t'') or ''u'' = ''u''(''x'', ''y'', ''t'') is a [[scalar function]] defined on the line or the plane, ''r'' is a real [[Bifurcation theory|bifurcation]] parameter, and ''N''(''u'') is some smooth nonlinearity.

The equation is named after the authors of the paper,<ref>{{cite journal|author=J. Swift |author2=P.C. Hohenberg |title=Hydrodynamic fluctuations at the convective instability|journal=Phys. Rev. A |volume=15|pages=319–328|year=1977|issue=1 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.15.319|bibcode=1977PhRvA..15..319S }}</ref> where it was derived from the equations for thermal [[convection]].

Another example where the equation appears is in the study of wrinkling morphology and pattern selection in curved elastic bilayer materials.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Stoop |first=Norbert |last2=Lagrange |first2=Romain |last3=Terwagne |first3=Denis |last4=Reis |first4=Pedro M. |last5=Dunkel |first5=Jörn |date=March 2015 |title=Curvature-induced symmetry breaking determines elastic surface patterns |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nmat4202 |journal=Nature Materials |language=en |volume=14 |issue=3 |pages=337–342 |doi=10.1038/nmat4202 |issn=1476-1122|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lewin |first=Sarah |date=8 April 2015 |title=A Grand Theory of Wrinkles |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/wrinkles-and-dimples-obey-simple-rules-20150408/ |website=[[Quanta Magazine]]}}</ref>

The Swift–Hohenberg equation leads to the [[Ginzburg–Landau equation]].
